ownerSurface: Test-owned SCHEMA-01 completeness fixture checked by scripts/schema-completeness.test.mjs and the internal/app/schemacompleteness tests; it is not a public contract or a second schema authority.
authoring: Directions and variants are authored from the native structure registry and command routes. Native-owned dispositions are authored from native admission and producer sources: the route call graph, the class indicators below, curated owners and committed native residue probes. schemaExpresses was recorded from the native structure owners and is re-derived from the published schemas by the oracle. Edit this file deliberately; no tool regenerates it.

schemaExpressedClasses.cardinality: contains, maxContains, maxItems, maxProperties, minContains, minItems or minProperties anywhere in a variant document
schemaExpressedClasses.bound: exclusiveMaximum, exclusiveMinimum, maxLength, maximum, minLength, minimum, multipleOf or pattern
schemaExpressedClasses.crossField: a relation between two or more members of one object: dependentRequired; dependentSchemas; if with then or else over two or more member names; or oneOf or anyOf with at least two object alternatives that together constrain two or more member names. A not that excludes values of one location relates no members.

nativeOwnedClasses.cardinality: Native item, member or entry counts (non-empty, at least, at most, exactly) of the document.
nativeOwnedClasses.bound: Native length, byte, numeric range and grammar limits (stable identifiers, repository-relative paths, digests).
nativeOwnedClasses.default: Native meaning of an omitted or null member: required presence, defaults and absence semantics of members the published schema leaves optional.
nativeOwnedClasses.duplicate: Native duplicate refusal: duplicate JSON member names, item, identity-key or normalized uniqueness and canonical ordering.
nativeOwnedClasses.enum: Native admitted value sets and literals.
nativeOwnedClasses.crossField: Native relations between members of one document: conditional presence, state and count agreement, mode or flag coupling.
nativeOwnedClasses.referenceClosure: Identifiers or pointers that must resolve to records declared elsewhere in the same document or in a fixed native catalog.
nativeOwnedClasses.numericCanonical: Input: exact canonical int64 token spelling and range that JSON Schema type integer does not distinguish (1, 1.0, 1e0). Output: the JSON number grammar of every emitted number token (stablejson.writeValue); the canonical integer spelling of an output number is a property of its producer.
nativeOwnedClasses.secretTimestamp: Secret-shaped, credential or timestamp-like text refusal or redaction.
nativeOwnedClasses.semantic: Native semantic admission or production: normalization, policy evaluation, digests and safety predicates. Always native.

dispositions: Each native-owned class of a direction is "absent" or a nonempty list of owner ids, every one statically reachable from the route handler. Input: owners are native functions reachable from the route whose static call closure reaches a refusal indicator of the class (default and semantic owners: reachability and any recorded witness); only mutation witnesses prove that the owner enforces the class (a verified lower bound, not exhaustive; the schema may express part of them). "absent" means no class indicator is reachable from the route handler; for default it also means the published input has no optional member. Output: the route producers (role producer) own every constraint of the output, which the schema describes; enforcers that the producer path also runs are listed with them. An output class is "absent" only where it cannot apply: duplicate without a published array, numericCanonical without a published number.

witnessKinds.test: A Go test in the owner package that statically reaches the owner (VTA) and spells evidence, a complete verb-free segment of a refusal literal of the owner that matches the class indicator.
witnessKinds.mutation: A Go test that fails when mutation.find, unique in the owner body, is replaced by mutation.replace (go test -overlay). This proves the test exercises that refusal of the owner.
witnessKinds.cli: A committed native residue row runs the route CLI on a schema-admitted perturbation of a recorded native observation; the native refusal contains evidence, a refusal literal segment of the owner.
witnessKinds.reachabilityOnly: A disposition none of whose owners carries a witness for the class: the owners are reachable from the route handler, and nothing proves that they enforce the class for this direction.

nonClaims: The published schemas never become semantic or policy authority: the manifest records which constraint classes stay native-owned and does not make any published schema a semantic or policy validator. Native admission stays authoritative and may refuse values a schema admits; the committed residue rows replay such refusals.

Native-owned records are a verified lower bound, not an inventory. Every named owner is reachable by Rapid Type Analysis from the route-sensitive slice of internal/app for its direction's route. Every input owner and every output enforcer named for cardinality, bound, duplicate, enum, unknownField, crossField, referenceClosure, numericCanonical or secretTimestamp reaches an indicator of that class through static calls; a mutation witness additionally ties its owner to the class by a refusal proof. Output producers own every class of their output by role. Default and semantic records are tied by reachability and, where one is recorded, by a witness; witnessSummary counts the reachability-only records. Reachability proves that an owner can run for the route, not that it runs for every input or member.

"absent" is relative to the class indicators. An input class is "absent" only when no indicator of the class is reachable by Rapid Type Analysis from the route: no function under classIndicators.scopes whose refusal literals match the class pattern and no named indicator helper. For default it also requires that the published input has no optional member. An output class is "absent" only where it cannot apply (see dispositions).

A test or cli witness shows one refusal whose text the owner spells; it does not prove exhaustive native behaviour. Test, cli and residue attribution is by an evidence substring of the owner's refusal literals: another function reachable from the same route may spell the same text, so the substring does not prove which function refused. A test witness is a literal tie; only mutation witnesses are refusal proofs, and they cover the sample named in this manifest. A cli witness is the only witness that runs through the route itself.

Unclassified reachable refusal sites: indicators classify refusal literals (prose and snake_case rule codes) by text. A reachable refusal whose literal matches no indicator, whose message is built in a composite literal or message table, or that refuses on a branch without a message literal belongs to no class, so an "absent" record does not exclude it.

Shared-literal ties: the indicator literal that ties an owner to a class may also match the indicators of other classes, so the tie does not show which class the owner enforces; only a mutation witness proves the named refusal.

Executed refusal sites not named as owners: owner lists are a lower bound, so a refusal site that the replayed input observations execute need not be named as an owner of any class of its direction. The execution cross-check proves only that every executed function lies in the route's reach set.

Observations without argv are admitted by their published variants under Ajv only and are not reproduced from committed inputs: the 104 output and 4 input rows below index 207 (input rows 0, 2, 128, 190), recorded at the lane commit 669ee3f, which is not on the published history, and the 33 appended output rows listed in the observation non-claims.

Non-unique residue evidence: a residue row's evidence is not checked to be unique among the refusal literals reachable from its route, so the row proves that the route refuses with that text, not that the named owner refused.
Output dispositions record that the producer owns every constraint of the output; they do not claim producer-side refusal.

Order-free raw-equality lists that uniqueItems could state exactly (obligation-decision candidateStates; requirement-context-slice nodeIds, requirementIds, ownerIds and lifecycleStates) stay native-owned duplicate constraints: both are projected through jsonshape, which has no uniqueness node, and a hand-added uniqueItems would split that single declaration. Overturn when a consumer needs structural duplicate detection on one of them: add a jsonshape uniqueness node whose admission and projection agree, and prove agreement with the committed uniqueItems agreement rows.
